audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Lillia,Skill,Olaf,Olaf,Lillia,Olaf,Olaf. The packet chart and the already-applied mirror both give Olaf,Skill,Skill,Lillia,Skill,Lillia,Skill — six of seven rows differ.
audit.why: Level 1 was given to Lillia, contradicting the page's own whys[0] ('Your Q-slow into auto wins first contact'), and levels 4-5 were given to Olaf, contradicting whys[3] ('Her spike'). Every row the prose describes correctly, the side token got backwards.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs to Olaf, Skill, Lillia, Skill, Lillia, Skill; ratings rescaled 7/5/5/4/5/4/5. whys[4] reworded so the level-6 row reads as a window rather than a guaranteed win.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page invents a mechanic Lillia does not have. Thirteen strings describe her W as a 'bounce' and five of those call it a heal — 'W healing-bounce', 'W (healing bounce)', 'bounce-heal', 'her W and E heal and reset', 'before her W bounce heals'. Riot's text for Watch Out! Eep! is one sentence: 'Lillia deals damage in a nearby area, dealing heavy damage in the center.' No bounce, no heal, and no heal flag on any slot of her kit. Separately, Lilting Lullaby's 150/130/110s cooldown is never given, and the page never states that her R only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust.
audit.why: This is the worst kind of error for a player: it tells them to disengage and wait out a heal that never happens, when the correct read is to keep swinging because nothing she has restores health. It also mis-sells her threat — her actual pressure is Blooming Blows' stacking move speed (down to 4s at rank 5) plus Swirlseed's slow, which is a kiting problem, not a sustain problem, and the counterplay is opposite. The Dream Dust prerequisite is the single most useful fact in the matchup: if she has not landed a spell on you, her 150-second ultimate cannot sleep you at all.
audit.corrected: Every heal/bounce claim replaced with the real kit — Blooming Blows' move-speed stacking and Swirlseed's slow — across whys[3], whys[6], spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], content.early, content.mid and content.late. The Dream Dust prerequisite and the 150s cooldown written into spikes[1].text, wants.foe[1] and phases[4].why. Ragnarok's 'cleanses' rewritten as immunity-while-attacking per Riot's text.

edits.before: Lillia is an off-meta kiter up top, and the early game is yours. At Level 1 your Q-slow into autos beats her first contact — she has no point-blank trade, only passive DOT and a W bounce that needs to ramp. Throw Q to stick the slow, then walk her down before she can bounce away. Pick your axe back up to keep the slow chained. Don't chase her into her own minions where her W and E heal and reset; make her come to the wave and punish every step into your range.
edits.after: Lillia is an off-meta kiter up top, and the early game is yours. At Level 1 your Q-slow into autos beats her first contact — she has no point-blank trade, only passive DOT and Watch Out! Eep! on 14s. Throw Q to stick the slow, then walk her down before her move-speed stacks build. Pick your axe back up to keep the slow chained. Don't chase her into her own minions where Swirlseed rolls back into you; make her come to the wave and punish every step into range.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are her window: with W (the healing bounce) and E leveled she kites your Q misses, DOTs you with passive, and refuses the melee trade you need. If your axe whiffs, don't dry-chase — she'll bounce out and heal it back. Wait for 6: Ragnarok cleanses her R sleep, her W slow and E slow, and lets you commit a true-damage all-in she can't kite. That's your reset button — burn it on her R, then E her down before omnivamp falls off.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are her window: with Watch Out! Eep! and Swirlseed leveled she kites your Q misses, DOTs you with passive, and refuses the melee trade you need. If your axe whiffs, don't dry-chase — every spell she lands stacks her move speed further. Wait for 6: Ragnarok blanks Lilting Lullaby for as long as you keep swinging, and her sleep only takes on targets already carrying Dream Dust. Burn it on her commit, then Reckless Swing her down.

edits.before: This evens out and then slips. From 2+ items a Liandry/Riftmaker Lillia out-skirmishes flat-true-damage Olaf — her DOT and bounce-heal win the extended fight your short combo can't close. Your job is to have already converted the early lead into plates, dives, and objectives. In teamfights you can still Ragnarok-dive her backline, but the clean 1v1 sustain race tilts to her once her items online. Don't let this go to a coinflip skirmish at three items.

notes: Biggest fabrication found in this slice: Lillia's W is described across thirteen strings as a bouncing heal. Riot's text is 'Lillia deals damage in a nearby area, dealing heavy damage in the center' — no bounce, no heal, and no heal flag anywhere in her kit. The page was telling players to break off a winning trade to wait out sustain that does not exist. I corrected every string where the heal was explicit; a few incidental 'bounce' mentions remain in strings I did not otherwise need to touch. Also worth a wider look: this reads like Lillia's kit description was confused with a different champion's, so any other Lillia page in the repo is suspect. Lillia is female and dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].t, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, tradeGood and several report entries call her 'he'/'his'.
